content_html:
PyTorch 2.14 ships with 2,995 commits from 487 contributors, headlined by NVGEMM (CuTeDSL-generated CUTLASS kernels with epilogue fusion for Inductor), a new nccl2 distributed backend ported from torchcomms with fault-tolerant process-group reconfiguration and one-sided RMA windows, and native linear algebra on Apple Silicon (SVD, eigh, QR, Cholesky). Compiler additions include torch.switch for multi-way branching, CUDA-graph-capturable torch.while_loop, and declarative dynamic shapes via @dynamic_spec shared across compile, export, and make_fx. Platform support expands with ROCm 7.14, Intel XPU native graph capture, Rubin (sm_107) targeting, and experimental torch.compile support for complex-valued tensors. Python 3.15 (including free-threaded 3.15t) gets eager-mode wheels, but torch.compile is not yet supported under 3.15 and raises a RuntimeError if invoked. TorchVision 0.29 is now ABI stable against future torch versions, decoupling its release cadence from PyTorch's.

Questions this post answers

What's new in the PyTorch 2.14 release for distributed training?

PyTorch 2.14 introduces a new nccl2 c10d backend ported in-tree from torchcomms, implementing the full collective Work contract with nonblocking communicators, eager communicator splitting, one-sided RMA windows, and suspend/resume memory offload. Fault tolerance also becomes a first-class c10d concept, letting a process group be reconfigured in place instead of torn down and restarted after a rank failure, and Flight Recorder now works across any backend, not just NCCL. Teams rolling out large-cluster training upgrades can track distributed PyTorch changes like this on daily.dev.

Does torch.compile work with Python 3.15 in PyTorch 2.14?

No, torch.compile is not supported under Python 3.15 in PyTorch 2.14; calling it raises a RuntimeError instead of silently falling back. Python 3.15 support in this release, including the free-threaded 3.15t build, is eager-mode only, so workloads depending on torch.compile should stay on Python 3.14 or earlier until Dynamo support for 3.15 lands. Anyone planning a Python or PyTorch upgrade can check compatibility gaps like this one on daily.dev before migrating.

What is NVGEMM in PyTorch 2.14 and how does it improve GEMM performance?

NVGEMM is a CuTeDSL-generated CUTLASS GEMM backend for TorchInductor that now supports epilogue fusion, so operations like bias adds, activations, and rescales after a matmul fuse into the same kernel instead of re-reading the result from memory in a separate kernel. It competes with Triton and ATen for mm, addmm, and scaled_mm, extends fusion to low-precision NVFP4 paths on Blackwell GPUs, and caches fused kernels to disk to avoid recompilation. Developers tuning GPU matmul performance can follow backend changes like NVGEMM's evolution on daily.dev.
